hypothesis.statement: enforce-allowed-paths.mjs and scope-expansion-gate.mjs both false-positive on a shared work branch because they diff baseSha...HEAD, which includes every unrelated commit landed since baseSha; preferring the union of a task's recorded execution.changedPaths across its iteration records, falling back to the commit-range diff only when no iteration has run yet, removes the false positives without requiring per-task branch isolation.

intendedChanges: Add tools/remediation/scope/recorded-changed-paths.mjs that unions execution.changedPaths across a task's iteration directory (governance/remediation/iterations/<taskId>/*.json), with unit tests.
Wire recordedChangedPaths as the preferred file list in enforce-allowed-paths.mjs, falling back to the existing baseSha...HEAD diff when no iteration has run yet.
Wire the same preference into scope-expansion-gate.mjs per scanned task contract.

Verify GAP-0003's completed contract (the task that originally surfaced 13 false violations) now passes with zero violations, and that the BASE_SHA_UNREACHABLE fallback still fires for a task with no recorded iterations and an unreachable baseSha.
forbiddenChanges: Weakening or removing the scope check itself.
Requiring per-task branch isolation as a precondition for this fix.

newFindings: guard-registry-gate.mjs's remediation-file exception is path-based, not name-based, so it needed no change for Wave R; by contrast these two scope tools key entirely off a commit-range diff, which is why they broke under a shared work branch while guard-registry-gate.mjs did not.

blindSpotsFound: Real per-task branch isolation (wave P0-E's Agent Controller, still human-gated) remains the more complete long-term fix; recordedChangedPaths is a correct and sufficient interim fix for the current shared-work-branch operating mode, but it depends on the executor accurately recording execution.changedPaths in every iteration, which is currently a convention, not itself schema-enforced against the actual git diff.
